Twentieth Amendment to the Constitution
31
Article 155A of the Constitution is hereby amended
by the repeal of paragraph (1) of that Article, and
the  substitution  therefor  of  the  following
paragraph:-
“(1)  There shall be a National Police
Commission (in this Chapter referred to as
the  “Commission”)  consisting  of  not  less
than five members and not more than seven
members appointed by the President subject
to  the  provisions  of  Article  41A.  The
President shall appoint one member as the
Chairman of the Commission.”; and
by the repeal of paragraph (4) of that Article, and
the  substitution  therefor  of  the  following
paragraph: -
“(4) Every member of the Commission
shall hold office for a period of three years
from the date of his appointment, unless he
becomes  subject  to  any  disqualification
under paragraph (2) of this Article, or earlier
resigns from his office by writing addressed
to the President or is removed from office
by the President, or is convicted by a court
of  law  of  any  offence  involving  moral
turpitude or if a resolution for the imposition
of civic disability upon him has been passed
in terms of Article 81 or is deemed to have
vacated his office under paragraph (6) of
this Article.”.
